facts.text: In 1925, Crystal Lakes officially formed a not‑for‑profit association, turning the area into a quiet haven for families.
Farmland and woodland gradually gave way to a charming lakeside neighborhood with winding roads, modest homes, and a strong sense of togetherness.
Four glacier‑carved kettle lakes—Main, North, South, and Hidden—interconnect via natural channels, with Main Lake covering about 20 acres and reaching depths of 40 feet.
Developed around man‑made lakes in the 1960s, Crystal Lakes functions mainly as a residential area with private lake access for homeowners.
In 2008, the Bethel Township Board of Trustees received a $45,000 block grant to build a parking lot and gazebo at Crystal Lakes Park.
Crystal Lakes is part of the Springfield, Ohio Metropolitan Statistical Area in southwestern Clark County.
